newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares edge up in quiet trade, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares edge up in quiet trade, seen rising.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Monday but trading was quiet on Monday because of the U.S. Columbus Day holiday, traders said.
They forecast prices would rise further in the next few days.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose 2.54 percent to 186.37 on $20.28 million in volume.

"Today's price rise and the rise tomorrow are primarily due to expectations of a further growth," said Maxim Perlin, head of sales and trade at UFG. "But when New York opens tomorrow prices will correct."
"People are looking for good offers," said Martin Diggle from Brunswick. "It seems Western institutions remain better buyers of stock and Russians are better sellers."
"I am fairly positive for the market this week, we see better buying in general."
Gazprom was the gainer of the day with prices rising to $0.475 from $0.445 and Diggle said operators played on the difference in share prices on the Moscow and international markets.

"People still believe that the discount for domestic Gazprom shares is too great compared to the American Depositary Receipts price," Diggle said. "A lot of people are buying the domestic Gazprom stock because they feel that over time the discount between the domestic and the ADR will narrow."
He forecast a rise in Gazprom for the next several weeks.
Tatneft was traded at $34.50 after $32.00 at Friday's close, Lenenergo rose to $0.420 from $0.395, Rostelekom fell to $2.755 from $2.740 and Norilsk Nickel was $6.50 after $6.33.
